+"""Interactive conversational mode for the Agentic ODI CLI.
+
+The chat is a small terminal REPL around an OpenAI-compatible model and the
+Agentic ODI MCP server. It streams assistant text, executes MCP tool calls,
+and keeps the conversation history in memory for the duration of the session.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import asyncio
+import json
+import os
+from collections.abc import Callable
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from typing import Any, Literal, Protocol
+
+import typer
+from core import ODI_ASSISTANT_PROMPT
+from fastmcp import Client
+from openai import AsyncOpenAI
+
+DEFAULT_BASE_URL = "http://localhost:8001/v1"
+DEFAULT_API_KEY = "local"
+DEFAULT_MODEL = "local-tools-model"
+DEFAULT_MCP_URL = "http://localhost:8000/mcp"
+
+SYSTEM_PROMPT = (
+    ODI_ASSISTANT_PROMPT
+    + """
+
+You are running in a terminal chat. Use the available MCP tools to create and
+query Jobs, Steps, Desired Outcomes, and Customer Outcomes instead of inventing
+records or IDs. Follow the ODI outcome statement format and flag opportunity
+scores above 10 as underserved. Keep answers concise and readable as plain text.
+"""
+)
+
+HELP_TEXT = """Commands:
+  /help   Show this help
+  /clear  Clear the conversation history
+  /tools  List the MCP tools available to the assistant
+  /exit   Quit (also /quit)
+
+Anything else is sent to the ODI assistant."""
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class ChatConfig:
+    """Connection settings for an interactive chat session."""
+
+    base_url: str
+    api_key: str
+    model: str
+    mcp_url: str
+
+    @classmethod
+    def from_env(
+        cls,
+        *,
+        base_url: str | None = None,
+        api_key: str | None = None,
+        model: str | None = None,
+        mcp_url: str | None = None,
+    ) -> ChatConfig:
+        """Resolve explicit values first, then environment variables, then defaults."""
+        return cls(
+            base_url=base_url or os.getenv("AGENTIC_ODI_BASE_URL") or DEFAULT_BASE_URL,
+            api_key=api_key or os.getenv("AGENTIC_ODI_API_KEY") or DEFAULT_API_KEY,
+            model=model or os.getenv("AGENTIC_ODI_MODEL") or DEFAULT_MODEL,
+            mcp_url=mcp_url or os.getenv("AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL") or DEFAULT_MCP_URL,
+        )
+
+
+class ChatSessionLike(Protocol):
+    """The session surface the command handler needs."""
+
+    tool_names: list[str]
+
+    def clear(self) -> None: ...
+
+
+def _to_openai_tools(tools: list[Any]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
+    """Translate FastMCP tool definitions into OpenAI function schemas."""
+    return [
+        {
+            "type": "function",
+            "function": {
+                "name": tool.name,
+                "description": tool.description or "",
+                "parameters": tool.input_schema or {"type": "object", "properties": {}},
+            },
+        }
+        for tool in tools
+    ]
+
+
+def _normalize_tool_calls(entries: dict[int, dict[str, str]]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
+    """Turn the per-index streaming tool-call buffers into OpenAI tool calls."""
+    return [
+        {
+            "id": entry["id"] or f"call_{index}",
+            "type": "function",
+            "function": {
+                "name": entry["name"],
+                "arguments": entry["arguments"] or "{}",
+            },
+        }
+        for index, entry in entries.items()
+    ]
+
+
+def _tool_result_text(result: Any) -> str:
+    """Extract readable text from an MCP tool result."""
+    content = getattr(result, "content", None) or []
+    parts = [getattr(item, "text", None) for item in content]
+    text = "\n".join(part for part in parts if part)
+    return text or str(result)
+
+
+def handle_command(line: str, session: ChatSessionLike) -> Literal["exit", "handled"] | None:
+    """Handle a slash command, or return None when the line is a chat message."""
+    command = line.strip().lower()
+    if command in {"/exit", "/quit"}:
+        return "exit"
+    if command == "/help":
+        typer.echo(HELP_TEXT)
+        return "handled"
+    if command == "/clear":
+        session.clear()
+        typer.echo("Conversation cleared.")
+        return "handled"
+    if command == "/tools":
+        if session.tool_names:
+            typer.echo("\n".join(session.tool_names))
+        else:
+            typer.echo("No tools loaded.")
+        return "handled"
+    if command.startswith("/"):
+        typer.echo(f"Unknown command: {line}. Type /help for commands.")
+        return "handled"
+    return None
+
+
+class ChatSession:
+    """A streamed tool-calling conversation against an OpenAI-compatible model."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        config: ChatConfig,
+        openai_client: Any,
+        mcp_client: Any,
+        *,
+        on_tool: Callable[[str, dict[str, Any]], None] | None = None,
+    ) -> None:
+        self.config = config
+        self.openai_client = openai_client
+        self.mcp_client = mcp_client
+        self.on_tool = on_tool
+        self.messages: list[dict[str, Any]] = [{"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM_PROMPT}]
+        self.tools: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
+        self.tool_names: list[str] = []
+
+    async def initialize(self) -> None:
+        """Discover the MCP tools once and expose them to the model."""
+        tools = await self.mcp_client.list_tools()
+        self.tools = _to_openai_tools(tools)
+        self.tool_names = [tool["function"]["name"] for tool in self.tools]
+
+    def clear(self) -> None:
+        """Drop the conversation history but keep the system prompt and tools."""
+        self.messages = [{"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM_PROMPT}]
+
+    async def _stream_completion(
+        self, on_delta: Callable[[str], None] | None
+    ) -> tuple[str, dict[int, dict[str, str]]]:
+        stream: Any = await self.openai_client.chat.completions.create(
+            model=self.config.model,
+            messages=self.messages,
+            tools=self.tools or None,
+            tool_choice="auto" if self.tools else None,
+            stream=True,
+        )
+
+        content_parts: list[str] = []
+        tool_calls: dict[int, dict[str, str]] = {}
+
+        async for chunk in stream:
+            choices = getattr(chunk, "choices", None)
+            if not choices:
+                continue
+            delta = choices[0].delta
+            if delta is None:
+                continue
+            content = getattr(delta, "content", None)
+            if content:
+                content_parts.append(content)
+                if on_delta is not None:
+                    on_delta(content)
+            for tool_call in getattr(delta, "tool_calls", None) or []:
+                entry = tool_calls.setdefault(
+                    tool_call.index, {"id": "", "name": "", "arguments": ""}
+                )
+                if tool_call.id:
+                    entry["id"] = tool_call.id
+                function = getattr(tool_call, "function", None)
+                if function is not None:
+                    if function.name:
+                        entry["name"] = function.name
+                    if function.arguments:
+                        entry["arguments"] += function.arguments
+
+        return "".join(content_parts), tool_calls
+
+    async def _call_tool(self, call: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
+        name = call["function"]["name"]
+        raw_arguments = call["function"].get("arguments") or "{}"
+        try:
+            arguments = json.loads(raw_arguments)
+        except json.JSONDecodeError:
+            return f"Error: invalid JSON arguments for {name}: {raw_arguments}"
+        if not isinstance(arguments, dict):
+            return f"Error: arguments for {name} must be a JSON object"
+        if self.on_tool is not None:
+            self.on_tool(name, arguments)
+        try:
+            result = await self.mcp_client.call_tool(name, arguments)
+        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
+            return f"Error calling {name}: {exc}"
+        return _tool_result_text(result)
+
+    async def ask(self, text: str, on_delta: Callable[[str], None] | None = None) -> str:
+        """Send a message, execute any tool calls, and return the final text."""
+        checkpoint = len(self.messages)
+        self.messages.append({"role": "user", "content": text})
+        try:
+            while True:
+                content, tool_calls = await self._stream_completion(on_delta)
+                if not tool_calls:
+                    self.messages.append({"role": "assistant", "content": content})
+                    return content
+
+                normalized = _normalize_tool_calls(tool_calls)
+                self.messages.append(
+                    {"role": "assistant", "content": content or None, "tool_calls": normalized}
+                )
+                for call in normalized:
+                    result = await self._call_tool(call)
+                    self.messages.append(
+                        {
+                            "role": "tool",
+                            "tool_call_id": call["id"],
+                            "name": call["function"]["name"],
+                            "content": result,
+                        }
+                    )
+        except Exception:
+            del self.messages[checkpoint:]
+            raise
+
+
+def _print_tool(name: str, arguments: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
+    rendered = json.dumps(arguments, ensure_ascii=False)
+    if len(rendered) > 100:
+        rendered = rendered[:97] + "..."
+    typer.secho(f"  → {name} {rendered}", fg="bright_black", err=True)
+
+
+async def _run_chat(config: ChatConfig) -> int:
+    typer.echo("Agentic ODI · interactive")
+    typer.echo(f"model: {config.model}  ·  mcp: {config.mcp_url}")
+    typer.echo("Type /help for commands, /exit to quit.\n")
+
+    llm: Any | None = None
+    try:
+        async with Client(config.mcp_url) as mcp_client:
+            llm = AsyncOpenAI(
+                base_url=config.base_url,
+                api_key=config.api_key,
+                timeout=60.0,
+            )
+            session = ChatSession(config, llm, mcp_client, on_tool=_print_tool)
+            await session.initialize()
+
+            while True:
+                try:
+                    line = input("you › ").strip()
+                except EOFError:
+                    typer.echo()
+                    break
+                except KeyboardInterrupt:
+                    typer.echo("\nUse /exit to quit.")
+                    continue
+
+                if not line:
+                    continue
+
+                action = handle_command(line, session)
+                if action == "exit":
+                    break
+                if action == "handled":
+                    continue
+
+                typer.secho("odi › ", fg="green", bold=True, nl=False)
+                printed = False
+
+                def on_delta(piece: str) -> None:
+                    nonlocal printed
+                    printed = True
+                    typer.echo(piece, nl=False)
+
+                try:
+                    await session.ask(line, on_delta=on_delta)
+                except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
+                    typer.echo()
+                    typer.echo(f"Error: {exc}", err=True)
+                    continue
+                typer.echo()
+                if not printed:
+                    typer.echo("(no response)")
+    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
+        typer.echo(f"Error: could not start chat: {exc}", err=True)
+        typer.echo(
+            f"MCP server: {config.mcp_url} (`python -m mcp_server`)\n"
+            f"LLM endpoint: {config.base_url}",
+            err=True,
+        )
+        return 1
+    finally:
+        if llm is not None:
+            await llm.close()
+
+    typer.echo("Goodbye.")
+    return 0
+
+
+def run_chat(config: ChatConfig) -> None:
+    """Run the interactive chat until the user exits."""
+    try:
+        exit_code = asyncio.run(_run_chat(config))
+    except KeyboardInterrupt:
+        typer.echo("\nGoodbye.")
+        return
+    if exit_code:
+        raise typer.Exit(code=exit_code)

+class DirectionOption(str, Enum):
+    MINIMIZE = "minimize"

+class CategoryOption(str, Enum):
+    REVENUE_GROWTH = "revenue_growth"
+    COST_REDUCTION = "cost_reduction"

+    RISK_MITIGATION = "risk_mitigation"

+    COMPLIANCE = "compliance"
+    BRAND_REPUTATION = "brand_reputation"
+    OTHER = "other"
+
+
+def _parse_value_metrics(values: list[str] | None) -> list[dict[str, Any]] | None:
+    if not values:
+        return None
+    metrics: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
+    for raw in values:
+        try:
+            parsed = json.loads(raw)
+        except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
+            raise typer.BadParameter("must be valid JSON", param_hint="--value-metric") from exc
+        if not isinstance(parsed, dict):
+            raise typer.BadParameter("must be a JSON object", param_hint="--value-metric")
+        metrics.append(parsed)
+    return metrics
+
+

+def add(
+    ctx: typer.Context,
+    job_id: str = typer.Option(..., help="Job ID the outcome belongs to"),

+    object_of_control: str = typer.Option(..., "--object"),
+    statement: str = typer.Option(..., help="Full outcome statement"),

+    satisfaction: float = typer.Option(..., min=1.0, max=10.0),
+    category: CategoryOption = typer.Option(..., help="Business impact category"),  # noqa: B008
+    business_statement: str = typer.Option(..., help="Business value statement"),
+    contextual_clarifier: str | None = typer.Option(default=None),
+    step_id: str | None = typer.Option(default=None),
+    value_metric: list[str] | None = typer.Option(  # noqa: B008
+        None, "--value-metric", help="Value metric as a JSON object. Repeatable."
+    ),
+) -> None:
+    """Add a Customer Outcome with customer and business value."""
+    customer_value: dict[str, Any] = {
+        "direction": direction.value,
+        "unit_of_measure": unit_of_measure,
+        "object_of_control": object_of_control,
+        "statement": statement,
+        "importance": importance,
+        "satisfaction": satisfaction,
+    }
+    if contextual_clarifier:
+        customer_value["contextual_clarifier"] = contextual_clarifier
+    metrics = _parse_value_metrics(value_metric)
+    if metrics is not None:
+        customer_value["value_metrics"] = metrics
+    args: dict[str, Any] = {
+        "job_id": job_id,
+        "customer_value": customer_value,
+        "business_value": {
+            "category": category.value,

+"""Jobs-to-be-Done CLI subcommands."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import Any
+
+import typer
+
+from cli.backend import Backend
+
+jobs_app = typer.Typer(help="Manage Jobs-to-be-Done.")
+
+
+def _backend(ctx: typer.Context) -> Backend:
+    backend: Backend | None = ctx.obj
+    if backend is None:
+        typer.echo("Error: no backend configured", err=True)
+        raise typer.Exit(code=1)
+    return backend
+
+
+@jobs_app.command("add")
+def add(
+    ctx: typer.Context,
+    name: str = typer.Option(..., help="Job name"),
+    description: str | None = typer.Option(default=None, help="Job description"),
+) -> None:
+    """Add a new Job."""
+    args: dict[str, Any] = {"name": name}
+    if description is not None:
+        args["description"] = description
+    typer.echo(_backend(ctx).call("add_job", args))
+
+
+@jobs_app.command("list")
+def list_jobs(ctx: typer.Context) -> None:
+    """List all Jobs."""
+    typer.echo(_backend(ctx).call("get_jobs", {}))
+
+
+@jobs_app.command("get")
+def get(ctx: typer.Context, job_id: str = typer.Argument(..., help="Job ID")) -> None:
+    """Get a Job by ID."""
+    typer.echo(_backend(ctx).call("get_job", {"job_id": job_id}))
+
+
+@jobs_app.command("update")
+def update(
+    ctx: typer.Context,
+    job_id: str = typer.Argument(..., help="Job ID"),
+    name: str | None = typer.Option(default=None, help="New job name"),
+    description: str | None = typer.Option(default=None, help="New job description"),
+) -> None:
+    """Update an existing Job."""
+    args: dict[str, Any] = {"job_id": job_id}
+    if name is not None:
+        args["name"] = name
+    if description is not None:
+        args["description"] = description
+    typer.echo(_backend(ctx).call("update_job", args))
+
+
+@jobs_app.command("delete")
+def delete(
+    ctx: typer.Context,

+"""First-run onboarding: page fetch, HTML signal extraction, confirmation card, typed fallback."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import asyncio
+import fnmatch
+import hashlib
+import os
+import re
+import sys
+from collections.abc import Sequence
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any, Optional
+
+import httpx
+
+# ── PageSignals ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+
+class PageSignals:
+    """Extracted signals from a fetched page."""
+
+    __slots__ = ("title", "meta_description", "domain", "primary_user",
+                 "business_model", "core_problem", "current_focus", "confidence")
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        title: str,
+        meta_description: str,
+        domain: str | None,
+        primary_user: str | None,
+        business_model: str | None,
+        core_problem: str | None,
+        current_focus: str | None,
+        confidence: str | None,
+    ) -> None:
+        self.title = title
+        self.meta_description = meta_description
+        self.domain = domain
+        self.primary_user = primary_user
+        self.business_model = business_model
+        self.core_problem = core_problem
+        self.current_focus = current_focus
+        self.confidence = confidence
+
+    def __repr__(self) -> str:
+        return f"PageSignals(title={self.title!r}, domain={self.domain!r}, confidence={self.confidence!r})"
+
+
+# ── Keyword-based inference ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
+
+DOMAIN_KEYWORDS: dict[str, int] = {
+    "devtools": 3,
+    "error": 2,
+    "tracking": 1,
+    "monitoring": 1,
+    "sentry": 2,
+    "performance": 1,
+    "analytics": 1,
+    "optimization": 1,
+}
+
+CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD = 3
+
+
+def infer_baseline(signals: PageSignals) -> tuple[profile.Baseline, dict[str, int]]:
+    """Deterministic keyword-based inference from extracted page signals.
+
+    Returns a Baseline and a dict of per-domain keyword scores.
+    """
+    scores: dict[str, int] = {}
+    text = (signals.title or "") + " " + (signals.meta_description or "")
+    for keyword, weight in DOMAIN_KEYWORDS.items():
+        count = len(fnmatch.findall(keyword, text.lower()))
+        if count:
+            scores[keyword] = count * weight
+
+    top_keyword = max(scores, key=scores.get, default=None) if scores else None
+    confidence = "high" if top_keyword and scores[top_keyword] >= CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD else "low"
+
+    # Map domain from signals; fall back to empty string if none
+    domain = signals.domain or ""
+
+    return profile.Baseline(
+        schema_version=1,
+        source="url",
+        product_name=None,
+        product_url=None,
+        domain=domain,
+        primary_user=signals.primary_user,
+        business_model=signals.business_model,
+        core_problem=signals.core_problem,
+        current_focus=signals.current_focus,
+        confidence=confidence,
+    ), scores
+
+
+# ── URL signal fetching ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+
+UA = "agentic-odi/0.1.0"
+
+
+def fetch_signals(url: str, timeout: float = 8.0) -> tuple[PageSignals, bool]:
+    """Fetch *url* and extract PageSignals.
+
+    Returns (signals, low_confidence) where low_confidence=True means the
+    inference confidence was "low" (≤2 keyword matches) — the caller should
+    fall back to the typed path.
+    """
+    try:
+        response = httpx.get(url, timeout=timeout, headers={"User-Agent": UA})
+        response.raise_for_status()
+    except Exception:
+        # Fetch failure → typed path
+        return _default_signals(low_confidence=True)
+
+    signals = _extract_signals(response.text, response.url)
+    baseline, scores = infer_baseline(signals)
+    low_confidence = baseline.confidence == "low"
+    return baseline, low_confidence
+
+
+def _default_signals(low_confidence: bool = False) -> tuple[PageSignals, bool]:
+    return PageSignals(
+        title="",
+        meta_description="",
+        domain=None,
+        primary_user=None,
+        business_model=None,
+        core_problem=None,
+        current_focus=None,
+        confidence="low" if low_confidence else "high",
+    ), low_confidence
+
+
+def _extract_signals(html: str, url: str) -> PageSignals:
+    """Extract signals from HTML using stdlib html.parser."""
+
+    title = ""
+    meta_description = ""
+
+    # Simple regex-based extraction (no external parser dependency)
+    t = re.search(r"<title>([^<]*)</title>", html, re.IGNORECASE)
+    if t:
+        title = t.group(1).strip()
+
+    m = re.search(
+        r'<meta\s+name=["\']description["\']\s+content=["\']([^>]*)["\']',
+        html,
+        re.IGNORECASE,
+    )
+    if m:
+        meta_description = m.group(1).strip()
+
+    # Very simple domain extraction from the URL
+    from urllib.parse import urlparse
+    parsed = urlparse(url)
+    domain = parsed.hostname or None
+
+    # Simple primary_user and business_model extraction from title/meta
+    # (placeholder: derive from title tokens)
+    primary_user = None
+    business_model = None
+    core_problem = None
+    current_focus = None
+
+    # Compute confidence based on keyword scores
+    scores = {}
+    text = (title or "") + " " + (meta_description or "")
+    for keyword, weight in DOMAIN_KEYWORDS.items():
+        count = text.lower().count(keyword)
+        if count:
+            scores[keyword] = count * weight
+
+    top_keyword = max(scores, key=scores.get, default=None) if scores else None
+    confidence = "high" if top_keyword and scores[top_keyword] >= CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD else "low"
+
+    return PageSignals(
+        title=title,
+        meta_description=meta_description,
+        domain=domain,
+        primary_user=primary_user,
+        business_model=business_model,
+        core_problem=core_problem,
+        current_focus=current_focus,
+        confidence=confidence,
+    )
+
+
+# ── Confirmation card ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+
+CARD_LINES: tuple[str, ...] = (
+    "Based on the page you're visiting, we've detected the following:",
+    "",
+    "Product: <product_name>",
+    "Problem: <core_problem>",
+    "Business Model: <business_model>",
+    "",
+    "If this is correct, type the details below.",
+    "Otherwise, type your inputs manually.",
+    "",
+    "Product name:",
+    "Core problem:",
+    "Business model:",
+    "",
+    "Type 'done' to accept these defaults, or press enter for the typed path.",
+)
+
+HONESTY_CONTRACT_LINES: tuple[str, ...] = (
+    "(this is an experimental feature — no data is shared without your consent)",
+    "we don't publish dates or send reminders",
+    "open an issue if you have questions: https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/issues",
+    "http://localhost:8000/mcp",  # MCP endpoint for maintainers",
+)
+
+
+# ── Public API ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+
+__all__ = [
+    "PageSignals",
+    "infer_baseline",
+    "fetch_signals",
+    "CARD_LINES",
+    "HONESTY_CONTRACT_LINES",
+]
+
+def maybe_run_first_launch(*, no_onboard: bool = False, invoked_subcommand: str | None = None) -> None:
+    """Skip first-run onboarding if conditions are met.
+
+    Conditions that skip onboarding:
+    - baseline already exists
+    - no TTY (non-interactive: not stdin.isatty() or not stdout.isatty())
+    - --no-onboard flag passed
+    - invoked Subcommand is one that should not trigger onboarding
+    """
+    import sys
+
+    if no_onboard:
+        return
+
+    if baseline_exists():
+        return
+
+    # Non-interactive contexts skip the card
+    if not (sys.stdin.isatty() and sys.stdout.isatty()):
+        return
+
+    # Do not trigger onboarding for specific subcommands
+    if invoked_subcommand and invoked_subcommand in {"setup", "profile", "version", "help"}:
+        return
+
+    # Show the confirmation card (implementation-specific; this is a stub)
+    typer.echo("First-run onboarding card would appear here.")
+    typer.echo("".join(HONESTY_CONTRACT_LINES))

+"""Path resolution utilities for the agentic-odi CLI."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import os
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+
+def install_root() -> Path:
+    """Resolve the installation root directory.
+
+    Resolution order:
+    1. AGENTIC_ODI_INSTALL_DIR env var
+    2. XDG_DATA_HOME/agentic-odi (POSIX) or %LOCALAPPDATA%\\agentic-odi (Windows)
+    3. ~/.local/share/agentic-odi (POSIX fallback)
+    """
+    env_install = os.environ.get("AGENTIC_ODI_INSTALL_DIR")
+    if env_install:
+        return Path(env_install).resolve()
+
+    if sys.platform == "win32":
+        local_app_data = os.environ.get("LOCALAPPDATA")
+        if local_app_data:
+            return Path(local_app_data) / "agentic-odi"
+        return Path.home() / "AppData" / "Local" / "agentic-odi"
+
+    xdg_data_home = os.environ.get("XDG_DATA_HOME")
+    if xdg_data_home:
+        return Path(xdg_data_home) / "agentic-odi"
+
+    return Path.home() / ".local" / "share" / "agentic-odi"
+
+
+def bin_dir() -> Path:
+    """Resolve the binary directory.
+
+    Resolution order:
+    1. XDG_BIN_HOME (POSIX) or install_root()/bin (Windows)
+    2. ~/.local/bin (POSIX fallback)
+    """
+    if sys.platform == "win32":
+        return install_root() / "bin"
+
+    xdg_bin_home = os.environ.get("XDG_BIN_HOME")
+    if xdg_bin_home:
+        return Path(xdg_bin_home)
+
+    return Path.home() / ".local" / "bin"
+
+
+def config_dir() -> Path:
+    """Resolve the configuration directory.
+
+    Resolution order:
+    1. XDG_CONFIG_HOME/agentic-odi (POSIX)
+    2. ~/.config/agentic-odi (POSIX fallback)
+    3. %APPDATA%\\agentic-odi (Windows)
+    """
+    if sys.platform == "win32":
+        app_data = os.environ.get("APPDATA")
+        if app_data:
+            return Path(app_data) / "agentic-odi"
+        return Path.home() / "AppData" / "Roaming" / "agentic-odi"
+
+    xdg_config_home = os.environ.get("XDG_CONFIG_HOME")
+    if xdg_config_home:
+        return Path(xdg_config_home) / "agentic-odi"
+
+    return Path.home() / ".config" / "agentic-odi"
+
+
+def versions_dir() -> Path:
+    """Resolve the versions directory where installed versions are stored."""
+    return install_root() / "versions"
+
+
+def current_link() -> Path:
+    """Resolve the 'current' symlink path."""
+    return install_root() / "current"
+
+
+def state_file() -> Path:
+    """Resolve the update state file path."""
+    return install_root() / "update.json"
+
+
+def is_frozen() -> bool:
+    """Check if the application is running in a frozen/packaged state."""
+    return bool(getattr(sys, "frozen", False))
+
+
+def is_writable_dir(p: Path) -> bool:
+    """Check if the given path is a writable directory."""
+    try:
+        return p.is_dir() and os.access(p, os.W_OK)
+    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
+        return False

+"""Profile model, XDG config path, atomic load/save, and `setup`/`profile` Typer sub-app."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+import os
+from datetime import datetime, timezone
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import typer
+
+app = typer.Typer(name="profile", help="Profile management commands")
+
+BASELINE_FILE_NAME = "baseline.json"
+
+
+@dataclass
+class Baseline:
+    schema_version: int = 1
+    created_at: str | None = None
+    source: str | None = None
+    product_name: str | None = None
+    product_url: str | None = None
+    domain: str | None = None
+    primary_user: str | None = None
+    business_model: str | None = None
+    core_problem: str | None = None
+    current_focus: str | None = None
+    confidence: str | None = None
+
+    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
+        return {
+            "schema_version": self.schema_version,
+            "created_at": self.created_at,
+            "source": self.source,
+            "product_name": self.product_name,
+            "product_url": self.product_url,
+            "domain": self.domain,
+            "primary_user": self.primary_user,
+            "business_model": self.business_model,
+            "core_problem": self.core_problem,
+            "current_focus": self.current_focus,
+            "confidence": self.confidence,
+        }
+
+    @classmethod
+    def from_dict(cls, d: dict) -> Baseline:
+        kwargs = {k: v for k, v in d.items() if k in cls.__dataclass_fields__}  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
+        return cls(**kwargs)
+
+
+def config_dir() -> Path:
+    """Return the XDG config dir for agentic-odi.
+
+    Uses XDG_CONFIG_HOME if set; otherwise falls back to HOME/agentic-odi.
+    """
+    xdg = os.getenv("XDG_CONFIG_HOME")
+    if xdg:
+        return Path(xdg) / "agentic-odi"
+    home = Path(os.getenv("HOME", ""))
+    return home / "agentic-odi"
+
+
+def baseline_file() -> Path:
+    """Return the path to the baseline JSON file."""
+    return config_dir() / BASELINE_FILE_NAME
+
+
+def baseline_exists() -> bool:
+    """Return True if the baseline file exists and is parseable."""
+    return baseline_file().exists()
+
+
+def load_baseline() -> profile.Baseline | None:
+    """Load the baseline file, returning None if it does not exist.
+
+    Raises ValueError on unparseable JSON.
+    """
+    if not baseline_exists():
+        return None
+    try:
+        with open(baseline_file(), "r") as f:
+            data = json.load(f)
+    except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError) as e:
+        raise ValueError(f"Failed to parse baseline file: {e}") from e
+    return Baseline.from_dict(data)
+
+
+def save_baseline(b: Baseline) -> Path:
+    """Save the baseline atomically, setting created_at ISO-8601 UTC when None."""
+    cfg_dir = config_dir()
+    cfg_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    b = (
+        b
+        if b.created_at is not None
+        else Baseline(
+            **{k: v for k, v in b.to_dict().items() if k != "created_at"},
+            created_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"),
+        )
+    )
+    target = baseline_file()
+    tmp = target.with_name(target.name + ".tmp")
+    with open(tmp, "w") as f:
+        f.write(json.dumps(b.to_dict()))
+    os.replace(tmp, target)
+    return target
+
+
+def backup_baseline() -> Path | None:
+    """Copy the existing baseline file to a dated backup.
+
+    Returns the path of the backup file, or None if no existing file.
+    """
+    if not baseline_exists():
+        return None
+    import shutil
+    backup_path = baseline_file().with_name(
+        f"baseline.json.bak-{datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime('%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ')}"
+    )
+    shutil.copy2(baseline_file(), backup_path)
+    return backup_path

+"""Job-map Steps CLI subcommands."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import Any
+
+import typer
+
+from cli.backend import require_backend
+
+steps_app = typer.Typer(help="Manage Job-map Steps.")
+
+
+@steps_app.command("add")
+def add(
+    ctx: typer.Context,
+    job_id: str = typer.Option(..., help="Job ID the step belongs to"),
+    name: str = typer.Option(..., help="Step name"),
+    order: int = typer.Option(..., help="Step order"),
+) -> None:
+    """Add a Step to a Job."""
+    typer.echo(
+        require_backend(ctx).call("add_step", {"job_id": job_id, "name": name, "order": order})
+    )
+
+
+@steps_app.command("list")
+def list_steps(
+    ctx: typer.Context,
+    job_id: str = typer.Option(..., help="Job ID to list steps for"),
+) -> None:
+    """List the ordered Step map for a Job."""
+    typer.echo(require_backend(ctx).call("get_job_map", {"job_id": job_id}))
+
+
+@steps_app.command("get")
+def get(ctx: typer.Context, step_id: str = typer.Argument(..., help="Step ID")) -> None:
+    """Get a Step by ID."""
+    typer.echo(require_backend(ctx).call("get_step", {"step_id": step_id}))
+
+
+@steps_app.command("update")
+def update(
+    ctx: typer.Context,
+    step_id: str = typer.Argument(..., help="Step ID"),
+    name: str | None = typer.Option(default=None, help="New step name"),
+    order: int | None = typer.Option(default=None, help="New step order"),
+) -> None:
+    """Update an existing Step."""
+    args: dict[str, Any] = {"step_id": step_id}
+    if name is not None:
+        args["name"] = name
+    if order is not None:
+        args["order"] = order
+    typer.echo(require_backend(ctx).call("update_step", args))
+
+
+@steps_app.command("delete")
+def delete(
+    ctx: typer.Context,
+    step_id: str = typer.Argument(..., help="Step ID"),
+    yes: bool = typer.Option(False, "--yes", "-y", help="Skip confirmation"),
+) -> None:
+    """Delete a Step and its dependent Outcomes."""
+    if not yes:
+        confirm = typer.confirm(f"Delete step {step_id}?")
+        if not confirm:
+            raise typer.Exit()
+    typer.echo(require_backend(ctx).call("delete_step", {"step_id": step_id}))

+"""Self-update engine primitives (checksum, extraction, atomic version swap)."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import hashlib
+import json
+import os
+import platform
+import shutil
+import tarfile
+import tempfile
+import urllib.request
+import zipfile
+from collections.abc import Callable
+from pathlib import Path
+from urllib.parse import urlparse
+
+from cli import paths
+from cli.version import __version__
+
+RELEASES_API = "https://api.github.com/repos/alehar9320/agentic-odi/releases/latest"
+CHECK_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 86400
+_RELEASES_DOWNLOAD = "https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/releases/download"
+
+_SYSTEM_MAP = {"Linux": "linux", "Darwin": "macos", "Windows": "windows"}
+_ARCH_MAP = {
+    "x86_64": "x86_64",
+    "AMD64": "x86_64",
+    "arm64": "arm64",
+    "aarch64": "arm64",
+}
+
+
+class UpdateError(Exception):
+    """Raised when an update cannot be performed."""
+
+
+def parse_version(s: str) -> tuple[int, int, int]:
+    """Parse a version string into a ``(major, minor, patch)`` tuple."""
+    cleaned = s.strip().lstrip("v")
+    parts = cleaned.split(".")[:3]
+    nums = [int(p) for p in parts]
+    while len(nums) < 3:
+        nums.append(0)
+    return (nums[0], nums[1], nums[2])
+
+
+def is_newer(latest: str, current: str) -> bool:
+    """Return True if ``latest`` is strictly newer than ``current``."""
+    return parse_version(latest) > parse_version(current)
+
+
+def asset_name(version: str, os_name: str, arch: str) -> str:
+    """Return the release asset filename for a version/platform combination."""
+    ext = "zip" if os_name == "windows" else "tar.gz"
+    return f"odi_{version}_{os_name}_{arch}.{ext}"
+
+
+def current_platform() -> tuple[str, str]:
+    """Map the running host to the release ``(os, arch)`` identifiers."""
+    os_name = _SYSTEM_MAP.get(platform.system(), platform.system().lower())
+    arch = _ARCH_MAP.get(platform.machine(), platform.machine().lower())
+    return os_name, arch
+
+
+def verify_checksum(path: Path, expected_hex: str) -> bool:
+    """Return True if the SHA-256 of ``path`` matches ``expected_hex``."""
+    digest = hashlib.sha256()
+    with path.open("rb") as handle:
+        for chunk in iter(lambda: handle.read(65536), b""):
+            digest.update(chunk)
+    return digest.hexdigest().lower() == expected_hex.strip().lower()
+
+
+def extract_archive(archive: Path, dest: Path) -> None:
+    """Extract ``archive`` (``.zip`` or ``.tar.gz``) into ``dest``."""
+    dest.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    if archive.name.endswith(".zip"):
+        with zipfile.ZipFile(archive) as zf:
+            zf.extractall(dest)  # nosec B202 - ZipFile strips absolute/'..' member paths
+    else:
+        with tarfile.open(archive, "r:gz") as tf:
+            tf.extractall(dest, filter="data")
+
+
+def _acquire_lock(install_root: Path) -> tuple[int, Path]:
+    lock_path = install_root / ".update.lock"
+    try:
+        fd = os.open(lock_path, os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | os.O_WRONLY)
+    except FileExistsError as exc:
+        raise UpdateError("update already in progress") from exc
+    return fd, lock_path
+
+
+def _activate_version(version_dir: Path, install_root: Path) -> None:
+    current = install_root / "current"
+    if os.name == "nt":
+        marker_tmp = install_root / "current.tmp"
+        if marker_tmp.exists() or marker_tmp.is_symlink():
+            marker_tmp.unlink()
+        marker_tmp.write_text(str(version_dir))
+        os.replace(marker_tmp, current)
+        return
+
+    tmp_link = install_root / "current.tmp"
+    if tmp_link.is_symlink() or tmp_link.exists():
+        tmp_link.unlink()
+    os.symlink(version_dir, tmp_link)
+    os.replace(tmp_link, current)
+
+
+def perform_update(
+    version: str,
+    archive_path: Path,
+    expected_sha: str,
+    install_root: Path,
+) -> Path:
+    """Verify, extract, and atomically activate ``version``; return its dir."""
+    install_root = Path(install_root)
+    versions = install_root / "versions"
+    versions.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+
+    lock_fd, lock_path = _acquire_lock(install_root)
+    try:
+        if not verify_checksum(archive_path, expected_sha):
+            raise UpdateError(f"checksum mismatch for {archive_path.name}")
+
+        tmp_dir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix=".extract-", dir=versions))
+        final_dir = versions / version
+        try:
+            extract_archive(archive_path, tmp_dir)
+            if final_dir.is_symlink() or final_dir.is_file():
+                final_dir.unlink()
+            elif final_dir.is_dir():
+                shutil.rmtree(final_dir)
+            os.replace(tmp_dir, final_dir)
+        except BaseException:
+            shutil.rmtree(tmp_dir, ignore_errors=True)
+            raise
+
+        _activate_version(final_dir, install_root)
+        return final_dir
+    finally:
+        os.close(lock_fd)
+        try:
+            lock_path.unlink()
+        except FileNotFoundError:
+            pass
+
+
+def should_check(state_file: Path, now: float) -> bool:
+    """Return True if an update check is due (missing/corrupt state ⇒ due)."""
+    try:
+        data = json.loads(Path(state_file).read_text())
+        last_check = float(data["last_check"])
+    except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError, TypeError):
+        return True
+    return (now - last_check) >= CHECK_INTERVAL_SECONDS
+
+
+def record_check(state_file: Path, now: float) -> None:
+    """Persist the timestamp of the most recent check."""
+    path = Path(state_file)
+    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    path.write_text(json.dumps({"last_check": now}))
+
+
+def _require_https(url: str) -> None:
+    """Reject anything that is not plain HTTPS before it can be opened."""
+    if urlparse(url).scheme != "https":
+        raise UpdateError(f"refusing non-HTTPS URL: {url}")
+
+
+def _default_fetch(url: str) -> str:
+    _require_https(url)
+    with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=10) as response:  # nosec B310 - _require_https
+        return response.read().decode("utf-8")
+
+
+def _default_fetch_bytes(url: str) -> bytes:
+    _require_https(url)
+    with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=10) as response:  # nosec B310 - _require_https
+        return response.read()
+
+
+def latest_release(current: str, *, fetch: Callable[[str], str] | None = None) -> str | None:
+    """Return the latest release version if newer than ``current``, else None."""
+    fetcher = fetch if fetch is not None else _default_fetch
+    try:
+        payload = json.loads(fetcher(RELEASES_API))
+        tag = str(payload["tag_name"]).strip()
+    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
+        return None
+    latest = tag.lstrip("v")
+    if is_newer(latest, current):
+        return latest
+    return None
+
+
+def _parse_checksums(text: str, filename: str) -> str | None:
+    """Return the SHA-256 hex for ``filename`` from a sha256sum-format body."""
+    for line in text.splitlines():
+        parts = line.split()
+        if len(parts) >= 2 and parts[1] == filename:
+            return parts[0]
+    return None
+
+
+def download(
+    version: str,
+    dest_dir: Path,
+    *,
+    fetch_bytes: Callable[[str], bytes] | None = None,
+) -> Path:
+    """Download and verify the release archive for ``version``."""
+    fetcher = fetch_bytes if fetch_bytes is not None else _default_fetch_bytes
+    base = f"{_RELEASES_DOWNLOAD}/v{version}"
+    asset = asset_name(version, *current_platform())
+
+    try:
+        checksums = fetcher(f"{base}/checksums.txt").decode("utf-8")
+    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
+        raise UpdateError(f"failed to fetch checksums.txt: {exc}") from exc
+
+    expected = _parse_checksums(checksums, asset)
+    if expected is None:
+        raise UpdateError(f"no checksum entry for {asset}")
+
+    try:
+        payload = fetcher(f"{base}/{asset}")
+    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
+        raise UpdateError(f"failed to fetch {asset}: {exc}") from exc
+
+    dest_dir = Path(dest_dir)
+    dest_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    dest = dest_dir / asset
+    dest.write_bytes(payload)
+    if not verify_checksum(dest, expected):
+        raise UpdateError(f"checksum mismatch for {asset}")
+    return dest
+
+
+def auto_update_enabled(no_update: bool) -> bool:
+    """Return whether auto-update is enabled by the flag/env opt-outs."""
+    return (not no_update) and (not os.environ.get("AGENTIC_ODI_NO_UPDATE"))
+
+
+def maybe_auto_update(*, no_update: bool, now: float) -> str | None:
+    """Best-effort background update; never raises, returns new version or None."""
+    try:
+        if not auto_update_enabled(no_update):
+            return None
+        root = paths.install_root()
+        if not paths.is_frozen():
+            return None
+        if not paths.is_writable_dir(root):
+            return None
+        if (root / ".update.lock").exists():
+            return None
+        state = paths.state_file()
+        if not should_check(state, now):
+            return None
+        record_check(state, now)
+        version = latest_release(__version__)
+        if version is None:
+            return None
+        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="odi-update-") as tmp:
+            archive = download(version, Path(tmp))
+            digest = hashlib.sha256(archive.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
+            perform_update(version, archive, digest, root)
+        return version
+    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
+        return None

+def _id_from(text: str) -> str:

+    return json.loads(match.group(1))["id"]  # type: ignore[index]

+def test_local_backend_full_crud_round_trip(tmp_path):

+    backend = LocalBackend(db_path=db)
+    job_text = backend.call("add_job", {"name": "J", "description": "d"})
+    assert "created successfully" in job_text
+    import json
+    import re
+
+    job_id = json.loads(re.search(r"({.*})", job_text).group(1))["id"]  # type: ignore[union-attr]
+    backend.call("add_step", {"job_id": job_id, "name": "S", "order": 1})
+    backend.call(
+        "add_outcome",
+        {
+            "job_id": job_id,
+            "statement": "Min x",
+            "importance": 8.0,
+            "satisfaction": 4.0,
+        },
+    )
+    listed = backend.call("get_outcomes", {"job_id": job_id})
+    assert "Min x" in listed
+    assert json.loads(backend.call("get_jobs", {}))[0]["name"] == "J"

+
+def test_resolve_backend_warns_on_db_with_mcp(capsys):

+"""Tests for the interactive CLI chat."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import asyncio
+import re
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from typing import Any
+
+from typer.testing import CliRunner
+
+from cli.chat import (
+    ChatConfig,
+    ChatSession,
+    _normalize_tool_calls,
+    _to_openai_tools,
+    handle_command,
+)
+from cli.cli import app
+
+ANSI_ESCAPE = re.compile(r"\x1b\[[0-9;]*m")
+
+
+def _strip_ansi(text: str) -> str:
+    return ANSI_ESCAPE.sub("", text)
+
+
+def _config() -> ChatConfig:
+    return ChatConfig(
+        base_url="http://localhost:8001/v1",
+        api_key="local",
+        model="test-model",
+        mcp_url="http://localhost:8000/mcp",
+    )
+
+
+class _FakeSession:
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self.tool_names = ["add_job", "get_jobs"]
+        self.cleared = False
+
+    def clear(self) -> None:
+        self.cleared = True
+
+
+class _FakeStream:
+    def __init__(self, chunks: list[Any]) -> None:
+        self._chunks = list(chunks)
+
+    def __aiter__(self) -> _FakeStream:
+        return self
+
+    async def __anext__(self) -> Any:
+        if not self._chunks:
+            raise StopAsyncIteration
+        return self._chunks.pop(0)
+
+
+class _FakeCompletions:
+    def __init__(self, streams: list[_FakeStream]) -> None:
+        self._streams = list(streams)
+        self.calls: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
+
+    async def create(self, **kwargs: Any) -> _FakeStream:
+        self.calls.append(kwargs)
+        return self._streams.pop(0)
+
+
+class _FakeMCP:
+    def __init__(self, tools: list[Any], results: dict[str, str]) -> None:
+        self._tools = tools
+        self._results = results
+        self.calls: list[tuple[str, dict[str, Any]]] = []
+
+    async def list_tools(self) -> list[Any]:
+        return self._tools
+
+    async def call_tool(self, name: str, arguments: dict[str, Any]) -> Any:
+        self.calls.append((name, arguments))
+        return SimpleNamespace(content=[SimpleNamespace(text=self._results[name])])
+
+
+def _chunk(content: str | None = None, tool_calls: list[Any] | None = None) -> Any:
+    delta = SimpleNamespace(content=content, tool_calls=tool_calls)
+    return SimpleNamespace(choices=[SimpleNamespace(delta=delta)])
+
+
+def _make_session(
+    streams: list[_FakeStream], tools: list[Any], results: dict[str, str]
+) -> tuple[ChatSession, _FakeCompletions, _FakeMCP]:
+    completions = _FakeCompletions(streams)
+    openai_client = SimpleNamespace(chat=SimpleNamespace(completions=completions))
+    mcp = _FakeMCP(tools, results)
+    session = ChatSession(_config(), openai_client, mcp)
+    return session, completions, mcp
+
+
+def test_chat_help_lists_connection_options() -> None:
+    runner = CliRunner()
+    result = runner.invoke(app, ["chat", "--help"])
+
+    assert result.exit_code == 0
+    output = _strip_ansi(result.output)
+    assert "--base-url" in output
+    assert "--model" in output
+    assert "--mcp-url" in output
+
+
+def test_no_args_without_tty_prints_help() -> None:
+    runner = CliRunner()
+    result = runner.invoke(app, ["--no-update"])
+
+    assert result.exit_code == 0
+    assert "Usage" in _strip_ansi(result.output)
+
+
+def test_config_from_env_uses_variables(monkeypatch) -> None:
+    monkeypatch.setenv("AGENTIC_ODI_BASE_URL", "http://example.test/v1")
+    monkeypatch.setenv("AGENTIC_ODI_API_KEY", "secret")
+    monkeypatch.setenv("AGENTIC_ODI_MODEL", "custom-model")
+    monkeypatch.setenv("AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL", "http://example.test/mcp")
+
+    config = ChatConfig.from_env()
+
+    assert config == ChatConfig(
+        base_url="http://example.test/v1",
+        api_key="secret",
+        model="custom-model",
+        mcp_url="http://example.test/mcp",
+    )
+
+
+def test_config_explicit_values_win_over_env(monkeypatch) -> None:
+    monkeypatch.setenv("AGENTIC_ODI_MODEL", "from-env")
+
+    config = ChatConfig.from_env(model="from-flag")
+
+    assert config.model == "from-flag"
+
+
+def test_handle_command_routes_and_clears(capsys) -> None:
+    session = _FakeSession()
+
+    assert handle_command("hello", session) is None
+    assert handle_command("/exit", session) == "exit"
+    assert handle_command("/quit", session) == "exit"
+    assert handle_command("/help", session) == "handled"
+    assert handle_command("/tools", session) == "handled"
+    assert handle_command("/clear", session) == "handled"
+    assert session.cleared is True
+    assert handle_command("/nope", session) == "handled"
+
+    output = capsys.readouterr().out
+    assert "add_job" in output
+    assert "Unknown command" in output
+
+
+def test_to_openai_tools_translates_fastmcp_schema() -> None:
+    tool = SimpleNamespace(
+        name="add_job",
+        description=None,
+        input_schema={"type": "object", "properties": {"name": {"type": "string"}}},
+    )
+
+    assert _to_openai_tools([tool]) == [
+        {
+            "type": "function",
+            "function": {
+                "name": "add_job",
+                "description": "",
+                "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"name": {"type": "string"}}},
+            },
+        }
+    ]
+
+
+def test_normalize_tool_calls_fills_missing_id_and_arguments() -> None:
+    calls = _normalize_tool_calls({0: {"id": "", "name": "get_jobs", "arguments": ""}})
+
+    assert calls == [
+        {
+            "id": "call_0",
+            "type": "function",
+            "function": {"name": "get_jobs", "arguments": "{}"},
+        }
+    ]
+
+
+def test_session_streams_the_answer_and_executes_tool_calls() -> None:
+    tool_start = SimpleNamespace(
+        index=0,
+        id="call-1",
+        function=SimpleNamespace(name="add_job", arguments='{"name": '),
+    )
+    tool_arguments = SimpleNamespace(
+        index=0,
+        id=None,
+        function=SimpleNamespace(name=None, arguments='"Test"}'),
+    )
+    first = _FakeStream(
+        [
+            _chunk(content="Let me add that. ", tool_calls=[tool_start]),
+            _chunk(tool_calls=[tool_arguments]),
+        ]
+    )
+    second = _FakeStream([_chunk(content="Added the job.")])
+    tools = [
+        SimpleNamespace(
+            name="add_job",
+            description="Add a job",
+            input_schema={"type": "object", "properties": {"name": {"type": "string"}}},
+        )
+    ]
+    session, completions, mcp = _make_session(
+        [first, second], tools, {"add_job": '{"id": "job-1"}'}
+    )
+
+    asyncio.run(session.initialize())
+    pieces: list[str] = []
+    reply = asyncio.run(session.ask("Add a job named Test", on_delta=pieces.append))
+
+    assert reply == "Added the job."
+    assert "".join(pieces) == "Let me add that. Added the job."
+    assert mcp.calls == [("add_job", {"name": "Test"})]
+    assert completions.calls[0]["stream"] is True
+    assert any(
+        message.get("role") == "tool" and message.get("content") == '{"id": "job-1"}'
+        for message in session.messages
+    )
+
+
+def test_session_rolls_back_failed_turn() -> None:
+    class _BoomCompletions:
+        async def create(self, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
+            raise RuntimeError("boom")
+
+    openai_client = SimpleNamespace(chat=SimpleNamespace(completions=_BoomCompletions()))
+    session = ChatSession(_config(), openai_client, _FakeMCP([], {}))
+    before = list(session.messages)
+
+    try:
+        asyncio.run(session.ask("hello"))
+    except RuntimeError as exc:
+        assert str(exc) == "boom"
+    else:  # pragma: no cover - the fake always raises
+        raise AssertionError("expected RuntimeError")
+
+    assert session.messages == before
+
+
+def test_session_clear_drops_history() -> None:
+    session, _, _ = _make_session([], [], {})
+    session.messages.append({"role": "user", "content": "hello"})
+
+    session.clear()
+
+    assert len(session.messages) == 1
+    assert session.messages[0]["role"] == "system"

+"""Tests for Customer Outcomes CLI commands."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+import re
+
+from typer.testing import CliRunner
+
+from cli.cli import app
+
+ANSI_ESCAPE = re.compile(r"\x1b\[[0-9;]*m")
+
+
+def _strip_ansi(text: str) -> str:
+    return ANSI_ESCAPE.sub("", text)
+
+
+_METRIC = (
+    '{"name":"m","direction":"minimize","unit_of_measure":"s","importance":6,"satisfaction":2}'
+)
+
+
+def _job_id(runner: CliRunner, db: str) -> str:
+    runner.invoke(app, ["--db", db, "jobs", "add", "--name", "J"])
+    return json.loads(runner.invoke(app, ["--db", db, "jobs", "list"]).output)[0]["id"]
+
+
+def _add_args(db: str, job_id: str, *extra: str) -> list[str]:
+    return [
+        "--db",
+        db,
+        "customer-outcomes",
+        "add",
+        "--job-id",
+        job_id,
+        "--direction",
+        "minimize",
+        "--unit",
+        "time",
+        "--object",
+        "setup",
+        "--statement",
+        "Minimize setup time",
+        "--importance",
+        "8",
+        "--satisfaction",
+        "4",
+        "--category",
+        "cost_reduction",
+        "--business-statement",
+        "Save hours",
+        *extra,
+    ]
+
+
+def test_customer_outcome_add_with_value_metrics(tmp_path):
+    db = str(tmp_path / "odi.db")
+    runner = CliRunner()
+    job_id = _job_id(runner, db)
+
+    result = runner.invoke(app, _add_args(db, job_id, "--value-metric", _METRIC))
+
+    assert result.exit_code == 0
+    assert '"name":"m"' in result.output
+    assert '"opportunity_score":10.0' in result.output
+
+
+def test_customer_outcome_add_rejects_bad_metric_json(tmp_path):
+    db = str(tmp_path / "odi.db")
+    runner = CliRunner()
+    job_id = _job_id(runner, db)
+
+    result = runner.invoke(app, _add_args(db, job_id, "--value-metric", "not-json"))
+
+    assert result.exit_code != 0
+    # Highlighted terminals (e.g. CI) split option tokens with ANSI codes, so
+    # strip styling before matching on the option name.
+    assert "value-metric" in _strip_ansi(result.output).lower()
+
+
+def test_customer_outcome_update_replaces_value_metrics(tmp_path):
+    db = str(tmp_path / "odi.db")
+    runner = CliRunner()
+    job_id = _job_id(runner, db)
+    created = runner.invoke(app, _add_args(db, job_id, "--value-metric", _METRIC))
+    outcome_id = json.loads(created.output.split(": ", 1)[1])["id"]
+    replacement = (
+        '{"name":"m2","direction":"maximize","unit_of_measure":"s","importance":9,"satisfaction":3}'
+    )
+
+    updated = runner.invoke(
+        app,
+        [
+            "--db",
+            db,
+            "customer-outcomes",
+            "update",
+            outcome_id,
+            "--value-metric",
+            replacement,
+        ],
+    )
+
+    assert updated.exit_code == 0
+    assert '"name":"m2"' in updated.output
+    assert '"name":"m"' not in updated.output
+
+
+def test_customer_outcome_list_get_delete(tmp_path):
+    db = str(tmp_path / "odi.db")
+    runner = CliRunner()
+    job_id = _job_id(runner, db)
+    created = runner.invoke(app, _add_args(db, job_id))
+    outcome_id = json.loads(created.output.split(": ", 1)[1])["id"]
+
+    listed = runner.invoke(app, ["--db", db, "customer-outcomes", "list", "--job-id", job_id])
+    assert outcome_id in listed.output
+
+    fetched = runner.invoke(app, ["--db", db, "customer-outcomes", "get", outcome_id])
+    assert json.loads(fetched.output)["job_id"] == job_id
+
+    deleted = runner.invoke(app, ["--db", db, "customer-outcomes", "delete", outcome_id, "-y"])
+    assert deleted.exit_code == 0 and "deleted successfully" in deleted.output

+    assert update.is_newer("0.1.0", "0.1.0") is False
+    assert update.is_newer("0.1.0", "0.2.0") is False
+

+def test_asset_name():
+    assert update.asset_name("0.1.0", "linux", "x86_64") == "odi_0.1.0_linux_x86_64.tar.gz"
+    assert update.asset_name("0.1.0", "windows", "x86_64") == "odi_0.1.0_windows_x86_64.zip"

+def test_current_platform_mapping(monkeypatch):
+    monkeypatch.setattr(update.platform, "system", lambda: "Darwin")
+    monkeypatch.setattr(update.platform, "machine", lambda: "arm64")
+    assert update.current_platform() == ("macos", "arm64")
+
+
+def _make_archive(tmp_path: Path, version: str) -> tuple[Path, str]:
+    payload = tmp_path / "stage" / version / "odi"
+    payload.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
+    payload.write_text("#!/bin/sh\necho odi")
+    archive = tmp_path / f"odi_{version}_linux_x86_64.tar.gz"
+    with tarfile.open(archive, "w:gz") as tf:
+        tf.add(payload.parent, arcname=".")
+    sha = hashlib.sha256(archive.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
+    return archive, sha
+
+
+def test_perform_update_flips_current(tmp_path):
+    archive, sha = _make_archive(tmp_path, "0.2.0")
+    root = tmp_path / "install"
+    version_dir = update.perform_update("0.2.0", archive, sha, root)
+    assert version_dir == root / "versions" / "0.2.0"
+    assert (root / "current").resolve() == version_dir.resolve()
+    assert (version_dir / "odi").exists()
+
+
+def test_perform_update_rejects_bad_checksum(tmp_path):
+    archive, _ = _make_archive(tmp_path, "0.2.0")
+    with pytest.raises(update.UpdateError):
+        update.perform_update("0.2.0", archive, "deadbeef", tmp_path / "install")
+    assert not (tmp_path / "install" / "current").exists()
+
+
+def test_verify_checksum(tmp_path):
+    p = tmp_path / "f"
+    p.write_bytes(b"hello")
+    good = hashlib.sha256(b"hello").hexdigest()
+    assert update.verify_checksum(p, good) is True
+    assert update.verify_checksum(p, "0" * 64) is False
+
+

+    archive = tmp_path / "evil.tar.gz"
+    with tarfile.open(archive, "w:gz") as tf:
+        info = tarfile.TarInfo(name="../escape.txt")
+        payload = b"pwned"
+        info.size = len(payload)
+        tf.addfile(info, io.BytesIO(payload))
+    dest = tmp_path / "out"
+    with pytest.raises((tarfile.TarError, update.UpdateError)):
+        update.extract_archive(archive, dest)
+    assert not (tmp_path / "escape.txt").exists()
+

+"""Map connector ingest records onto ODI evidence drafts.
+
+This module deliberately does not import the ODI store. It produces transport
+records shaped for ``core.Evidence``; the CLI (or any caller) owns persistence,
+so connector plumbing never leaks into the ODI repository.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import Any
+
+from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
+
+from connectors.models import EvidenceItemType, IngestBatch, IngestRecord
+
+
+class EvidenceDraft(BaseModel):
+    """An ingest record ready to become ODI evidence."""
+
+    source_name: str
+    source_kind: str
+    item_type: EvidenceItemType
+    name: str
+    content: str
+    raw: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)
+    job_id: str | None = None
+    step_id: str | None = None
+    outcome_id: str | None = None
+
+
+def drafts_from_batch(
+    batch: IngestBatch,
+    *,
+    job_id: str | None = None,
+    step_id: str | None = None,
+    outcome_id: str | None = None,
+    include_catalog: bool = False,
+) -> list[EvidenceDraft]:
+    """Turn every evidence-bearing record in ``batch`` into a draft.
+
+    Catalog records describe the connector itself and are skipped unless
+    ``include_catalog`` is set.
+    """
+    drafts: list[EvidenceDraft] = []
+    for record in batch.records:
+        if record.item_type == "catalog" and not include_catalog:
+            continue
+        drafts.append(_draft_from_record(record, job_id, step_id, outcome_id))
+    return drafts
+
+
+def _draft_from_record(
+    record: IngestRecord,
+    job_id: str | None,
+    step_id: str | None,
+    outcome_id: str | None,
+) -> EvidenceDraft:
+    return EvidenceDraft(
+        source_name=record.source_name,
+        source_kind=record.source_kind,
+        item_type=record.item_type,
+        name=record.name,
+        content=record.content,
+        raw=record.raw,
+        job_id=job_id,
+        step_id=step_id,
+        outcome_id=outcome_id,
+    )

+"""REST and webhook connector kinds.
+
+Both kinds share one HTTP puller: a REST endpoint returns a JSON document, and a
+webhook connector posts a configured request (usually to a webhook inbox or a
+subscription endpoint) and normalizes the JSON response. The transport is
+injectable so tests never touch the network.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+import urllib.request
+from collections.abc import Callable
+from typing import Any
+
+from connectors.models import (
+    HealthStatus,
+    IngestBatch,
+    IngestRecord,
+    RestConnectorSettings,
+)
+from connectors.protocol import Connector
+
+FetchResult = tuple[int, bytes]
+Fetcher = Callable[[str, str, dict[str, str], bytes | None, float], FetchResult]
+
+
+def _default_fetch(
+    method: str,
+    url: str,
+    headers: dict[str, str],
+    body: bytes | None,
+    timeout: float,
+) -> FetchResult:
+    request = urllib.request.Request(url, data=body, headers=headers, method=method)
+    with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=timeout) as response:  # nosec B310
+        return int(response.status), response.read()
+
+
+def _lookup(payload: Any, path: str) -> Any:
+    current = payload
+    for part in path.split("."):
+        if not isinstance(current, dict) or part not in current:
+            return None
+        current = current[part]
+    return current
+
+
+class RestConnector(Connector):
+    """Pulls JSON records from an HTTP endpoint into the ingest sink."""
+
+    kind = "rest"
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        name: str,
+        settings: RestConnectorSettings,
+        *,
+        kind: str | None = None,
+        fetcher: Fetcher | None = None,
+    ) -> None:
+        self.name = name
+        self.settings = settings
+        self.kind = kind or type(self).kind
+        self._fetch = fetcher or _default_fetch
+
+    def _request(self) -> FetchResult:
+        body = None
+        headers = dict(self.settings.headers)
+        if self.settings.json_body is not None:
+            body = json.dumps(self.settings.json_body).encode("utf-8")
+            headers.setdefault("Content-Type", "application/json")
+        return self._fetch(
+            self.settings.method,
+            self.settings.url,
+            headers,
+            body,
+            self.settings.timeout,
+        )
+
+    def _items(self, payload: Any) -> list[Any]:
+        if self.settings.records_key:
+            extracted = _lookup(payload, self.settings.records_key)
+            if isinstance(extracted, list):
+                return extracted
+        if isinstance(payload, list):
+            return payload
+        if isinstance(payload, dict):
+            for key in ("records", "items", "data"):
+                value = payload.get(key)
+                if isinstance(value, list):
+                    return value
+        return [payload]
+
+    def _record(self, item: Any, index: int) -> IngestRecord:
+        if isinstance(item, dict):
+            name = str(
+                item.get("name")
+                or item.get("title")
+                or item.get("id")
+                or f"{self.name}-{index + 1}"
+            )
+            content = None
+            for key in ("content", "text", "description", "body", "summary"):
+                if isinstance(item.get(key), str):
+                    content = item[key]
+                    break
+            if content is None:
+                content = json.dumps(item, indent=2, default=str)
+            raw = item
+        elif isinstance(item, str):
+            name = f"{self.name}-{index + 1}"
+            content = item
+            raw = {"value": item}
+        else:
+            name = f"{self.name}-{index + 1}"
+            content = json.dumps(item, default=str)
+            raw = {"value": item}
+        return IngestRecord(
+            source_name=self.name,
+            source_kind=self.kind,
+            item_type=self.settings.item_type,
+            name=name,
+            content=content,
+            raw=raw,
+        )
+
+    async def health(self) -> HealthStatus:
+        try:
+            status, _ = self._request()
+        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
+            return HealthStatus(ok=False, message=str(exc))
+        ok = 200 <= status < 400
+        return HealthStatus(
+            ok=ok,
+            message="reachable" if ok else f"HTTP {status}",
+            details={"status": status, "url": self.settings.url},
+        )
+
+    async def ingest(self) -> IngestBatch:
+        batch = IngestBatch(connector_name=self.name)
+        try:
+            status, body = self._request()
+        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
+            batch.errors.append(str(exc))
+            return batch
+        if not 200 <= status < 400:
+            batch.errors.append(f"HTTP {status} from {self.settings.url}")
+            return batch
+        text = body.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
+        try:
+            payload: Any = json.loads(text)
+        except json.JSONDecodeError:
+            payload = text
+        records = self._items(payload)
+        for index, item in enumerate(records):
+            batch.records.append(self._record(item, index))
+        return batch
+
+
+class WebhookConnector(RestConnector):
+    """Posts to a webhook endpoint and ingests the JSON response."""
+
+    kind = "webhook"

+from connectors.mapping import drafts_from_batch
+from connectors.models import IngestBatch, IngestRecord
+
+
+def _batch() -> IngestBatch:
+    return IngestBatch(
+        connector_name="gong",
+        records=[
+            IngestRecord(
+                source_name="gong",
+                source_kind="mcp",
+                item_type="catalog",
+                name="mcp-catalog",
+                content="{}",
+            ),
+            IngestRecord(
+                source_name="gong",
+                source_kind="mcp",
+                item_type="resource",
+                name="feedback",
+                content="Onboarding is slow",
+                raw={"uri": "resource://feedback"},
+            ),
+            IngestRecord(
+                source_name="gong",
+                source_kind="mcp",
+                item_type="tool_result",
+                name="latest_quote",
+                content="Lost two hours",
+            ),
+        ],
+    )
+
+
+def test_mapping_skips_catalog_by_default() -> None:
+    drafts = drafts_from_batch(_batch())
+
+    assert [draft.name for draft in drafts] == ["feedback", "latest_quote"]
+    assert all(draft.source_name == "gong" for draft in drafts)
+    assert drafts[0].raw == {"uri": "resource://feedback"}
+
+
+def test_mapping_can_include_catalog() -> None:
+    drafts = drafts_from_batch(_batch(), include_catalog=True)
+
+    assert [draft.name for draft in drafts] == ["mcp-catalog", "feedback", "latest_quote"]
+
+
+def test_mapping_attaches_odi_links() -> None:
+    drafts = drafts_from_batch(_batch(), job_id="j1", step_id="s1", outcome_id="o1")
+
+    assert all(draft.job_id == "j1" for draft in drafts)
+    assert all(draft.step_id == "s1" for draft in drafts)
+    assert all(draft.outcome_id == "o1" for draft in drafts)

+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+from typing import Any
+
+import pytest
+
+from connectors.models import RestConnectorSettings
+from connectors.rest.connector import RestConnector, WebhookConnector
+
+Calls = list[tuple[str, str, dict[str, str], bytes | None, float]]
+
+
+def _fetcher(status: int, payload: Any, calls: Calls | None = None):
+    def fetch(
+        method: str, url: str, headers: dict[str, str], body: bytes | None, timeout: float
+    ) -> tuple[int, bytes]:
+        if calls is not None:
+            calls.append((method, url, headers, body, timeout))
+        text = payload if isinstance(payload, str) else json.dumps(payload)
+        return status, text.encode("utf-8")
+
+    return fetch
+
+
+def _connector(payload: Any, status: int = 200, **settings: Any) -> RestConnector:
+    base: dict[str, Any] = {"url": "https://api.example/records"}
+    base.update(settings)
+    return RestConnector(
+        name="jira",
+        settings=RestConnectorSettings(**base),
+        fetcher=_fetcher(status, payload),
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_health_reports_reachable_on_2xx() -> None:
+    status = await _connector([]).health()
+
+    assert status.ok is True
+    assert status.message == "reachable"
+    assert status.details["status"] == 200
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_health_reports_http_failure() -> None:
+    status = await _connector([], status=503).health()
+
+    assert status.ok is False
+    assert "503" in status.message
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_ingest_normalizes_list_payload() -> None:
+    batch = await _connector([{"name": "ticket-1", "content": "Login fails"}]).ingest()
+
+    assert batch.errors == []
+    assert len(batch.records) == 1
+    record = batch.records[0]
+    assert record.name == "ticket-1"
+    assert record.content == "Login fails"
+    assert record.source_name == "jira"
+    assert record.source_kind == "rest"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_ingest_uses_records_key_and_serializes_objects() -> None:
+    payload = {"result": {"issues": [{"id": "ABC-1", "summary": "Slow deploy"}]}}
+    batch = await _connector(payload, records_key="result.issues").ingest()
+
+    assert len(batch.records) == 1
+    assert batch.records[0].name == "ABC-1"
+    assert batch.records[0].content == "Slow deploy"
+    assert batch.records[0].raw["id"] == "ABC-1"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_ingest_treats_plain_text_as_one_record() -> None:
+    batch = await _connector("customer says onboarding is slow").ingest()
+
+    assert len(batch.records) == 1
+    assert batch.records[0].content == "customer says onboarding is slow"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_ingest_records_fetch_errors() -> None:
+    def fetch(*_args: Any) -> tuple[int, bytes]:
+        raise ConnectionError("refused")
+
+    connector = RestConnector(
+        name="jira",
+        settings=RestConnectorSettings(url="https://api.example/records"),
+        fetcher=fetch,
+    )
+
+    batch = await connector.ingest()
+
+    assert batch.records == []

+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_webhook_posts_json_body_and_uses_configured_item_type() -> None:
+    calls: Calls = []
+    connector = WebhookConnector(
+        name="inbox",
+        settings=RestConnectorSettings(
+            url="https://hooks.example/inbox",
+            method="POST",
+            json_body={"query": "latest"},
+            item_type="tool_result",
+        ),
+        fetcher=_fetcher(200, {"records": [{"name": "quote", "content": "Too slow"}]}, calls),
+    )
+
+    batch = await connector.ingest()
+
+    method, url, headers, body, _timeout = calls[0]
+    assert (method, url) == ("POST", "https://hooks.example/inbox")
+    assert headers["Content-Type"] == "application/json"
+    assert body is not None and json.loads(body) == {"query": "latest"}
+    assert batch.records[0].source_kind == "webhook"

+"""Evaluate desired-outcome statements against the ODI format."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import Any
+
+_CONTEXT_MARKERS = (
+    " when ",
+    " while ",
+    " before ",
+    " after ",
+    " during ",
+    " if ",
+    " as ",
+)
+
+_VAGUE_TERMS = ("better", "improve", "optimize", "faster", "easier")
+
+
+def evaluate_outcome_statement(statement: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """Return format feedback for a desired-outcome statement."""
+    text = statement.strip()
+    lowered = text.lower()
+    padded = f" {lowered} "
+    issues: list[str] = []
+    suggestions: list[str] = []
+
+    direction: str | None = None
+    if lowered.startswith("minimize"):
+        direction = "minimize"
+    elif lowered.startswith("maximize"):
+        direction = "maximize"
+    else:
+        issues.append("Statement must start with 'Minimize' or 'Maximize'.")
+        suggestions.append("Start with 'Minimize/Maximize the [metric] ...'.")
+
+    if " the " not in padded:
+        issues.append("Name the object of control after 'the'.")
+        suggestions.append("Say what is being minimized or maximized, e.g. 'the time to ...'.")
+
+    if not any(marker in padded for marker in _CONTEXT_MARKERS):
+        issues.append("Add the execution context with 'when ...', 'while ...', or 'before ...'.")
+        suggestions.append("Close with the situation, e.g. '... when onboarding a new customer'.")
+
+    if len(text.split()) < 4:
+        issues.append("Statement is too short to describe a measurable outcome.")
+        suggestions.append("Describe the metric, the object, and the context.")
+
+    if len(text) > 200:
+        issues.append("Statement is longer than 200 characters; keep it to one measurable outcome.")
+        suggestions.append("Split broad statements into separate outcomes.")
+
+    vague = [term for term in _VAGUE_TERMS if term in lowered]
+    if vague:
+        issues.append(f"Replace vague terms with a measurable metric: {', '.join(vague)}.")
+        suggestions.append("Use a metric such as time, cost, effort, errors, or likelihood.")
+
+    return {
+        "statement": text,
+        "valid": not issues,
+        "direction": direction,
+        "issues": issues,
+        "suggestions": suggestions,
+    }

+"""Repository factory selecting a persistent or in-memory store."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import os
+
+from core.repository import InMemoryRepository, Repository
+from core.sqlite_repository import SQLiteRepository
+
+
+def build_repository(db_path: str | None = None) -> Repository:
+    resolved: str | None
+    if db_path is not None:
+        resolved = db_path
+    else:
+        resolved = os.environ.get("AGENTIC_ODI_DB")
+    if resolved is None:
+        resolved = os.path.expanduser("~/.agentic-odi/odi.db")
+    if resolved == ":memory:":
+        return InMemoryRepository()
+    parent = os.path.dirname(resolved)
+    if parent:
+        os.makedirs(parent, exist_ok=True)
+    return SQLiteRepository(db_path=resolved)

 import json
 import sqlite3
 from datetime import datetime
 
 
 class IntentStore:
-    def __init__(self, db_path: str = "intent_store.db") -> None:
+    def __init__(self, db_path: str = "intent_store.db", check_same_thread: bool = True) -> None:

-        self.conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path)
+        self.conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path, check_same_thread=check_same_thread)

     def _init_db(self) -> None:
         """Creates an immutable, append-only event table."""
         with self.conn:
             self.conn.execute(
                 """
                 CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS events (
                     id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
                     timestamp TEXT NOT NULL,
                     event_type TEXT NOT NULL,
                     payload TEXT NOT NULL
                 )
             """
             )
 
     def append(self, event_type: str, payload: dict) -> None:
         """Appends a new event to the stream (Immutable write)."""
         timestamp = datetime.utcnow().isoformat()
         payload_json = json.dumps(payload)
         with self.conn:
             self.conn.execute(
                 "INSERT INTO events (timestamp, event_type, payload) VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
                 (timestamp, event_type, payload_json),
             )
 
     def get_stream(self) -> list[dict]:
         """Retrieves the full chronological event stream for AI reasoning."""
         cursor = self.conn.cursor()
         cursor.execute("SELECT id, timestamp, event_type, payload FROM events ORDER BY id ASC")
         return [
             {
                 "id": row[0],
                 "timestamp": row[1],
                 "type": row[2],
                 "payload": json.loads(row[3]) if row[3] else {},
             }
             for row in cursor.fetchall()
         ]
 
     def clear(self) -> None:
         """Clear all events (for testing)."""
         with self.conn:
             self.conn.execute("DELETE FROM events")
 
     def close(self) -> None:
         self.conn.close()

 """Core domain models for Agentic ODI."""
 
 from __future__ import annotations
 
 import uuid
 from enum import Enum
+from typing import Any, Literal
 
 from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, computed_field
 
 
 class Direction(str, Enum):
     MINIMIZE = "minimize"
     MAXIMIZE = "maximize"
 
 
 class BusinessImpactCategory(str, Enum):
     REVENUE_GROWTH = "revenue_growth"
     COST_REDUCTION = "cost_reduction"
     RETENTION = "retention"
     RISK_MITIGATION = "risk_mitigation"
     OPERATIONAL_EFFICIENCY = "operational_efficiency"
     COMPLIANCE = "compliance"
     BRAND_REPUTATION = "brand_reputation"
     OTHER = "other"
 
 
 def compute_opportunity_score(importance: float, satisfaction: float) -> float:
     """ODI Opportunity Score = importance + max(importance - satisfaction, 0)."""
     return float(importance + max(importance - satisfaction, 0.0))
 
 
 class Job(BaseModel):
     id: str = Field(default_factory=lambda: str(uuid.uuid4()))

+"""Canonical JSON schemas for every ODI entity.
+
+These schemas are the machine-readable contract used by agents, connectors, and
+CLI consumers. They are derived from the Pydantic models so there is exactly one
+definition of the ODI dataset.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import Any
+
+from pydantic import BaseModel
+
+from core.models import (
+    BusinessValue,
+    CustomerOutcome,
+    CustomerValue,
+    Evidence,
+    Job,
+    Outcome,
+    Step,
+    ValueMetric,
+)
+
+_SCHEMA_MODELS: dict[str, type[BaseModel]] = {
+    "Job": Job,
+    "Step": Step,
+    "Outcome": Outcome,
+    "ValueMetric": ValueMetric,
+    "CustomerValue": CustomerValue,
+    "BusinessValue": BusinessValue,
+    "CustomerOutcome": CustomerOutcome,
+    "Evidence": Evidence,
+}
+
+
+def odi_schema() -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """Return the JSON schema for each ODI entity keyed by model name."""
+    return {name: model.model_json_schema() for name, model in _SCHEMA_MODELS.items()}

+        statement: str | None = None,
+        name: str | None = None,
+        importance: float | None = None,
+        satisfaction: float | None = None,
+    ) -> Job | Outcome:
+        evidence = self.repo.get_evidence(evidence_id)
+        if evidence is None:
+            raise EvidenceNotFoundError(evidence_id)
+        if target == "job":
+            label = (
+                (name or evidence.name).strip() or _first_line(evidence.content) or "Imported job"
+            )

+                or _first_line(evidence.content)
+                or "Untitled outcome"
+            )

+                satisfaction=satisfaction,

+            )

+from core import InMemoryRepository, build_repository

+    monkeypatch.setenv("AGENTIC_ODI_DB", str(env_path))

+

+    monkeypatch.setenv("AGENTIC_ODI_DB", str(env_path))
+    repo = build_repository()
+    assert isinstance(repo, SQLiteRepository)
+    assert env_path.exists()
+
+

+    repo = build_repository()
+    assert isinstance(repo, SQLiteRepository)
